t: Replace Elements with Greatest Element on Right Side
o: For each index we must output the maximum of all elements strictly to its right; the last position gets -1. In the example [17,18,5,4,6,1], index 0 becomes 18 (max of 18,5,4,6,1), index 1 becomes 6 (max of 5,4,6,1), and so on until index 5 which has nothing to its right and becomes -1. A single-element array like [400] immediately yields [-1]. With n up to 10^4, even an O(n^2) brute force would pass, but a single right-to-left pass with a running maximum gives O(n).
k: The answer for index i depends only on the running maximum of arr[i+1..n-1], so one right-to-left scan suffices.
Process from the end: keep maxSoFar initialized to -1, and at each step record the old value before overwriting it.
The last element is always -1, which falls out naturally if you start the scan with maxSoFar = -1.

a.i: For every index i, scan all elements to its right and take their maximum. This directly mirrors the problem definition. It is O(n^2) but fine given n <= 10^4.
s: For each i from 0 to n-2, compute max(arr[i+1..n-1]) and store it in the result.
Set the last element of the result to -1.
a.t: O(n^2) — each of the n positions scans up to n elements to its right.
a.sp: O(1) extra beyond the output array (or O(n) if a separate result array is counted).

a.i: Traverse from right to left while maintaining maxSoFar, the greatest element seen so far on the right side. The answer at index i is exactly the maxSoFar before including arr[i], so we save the old value, write it into arr[i], then update maxSoFar with arr[i]. Starting with maxSoFar = -1 automatically handles the last element.
s: Iterate i from n-1 down to 0.
Save temp = arr[i]; set arr[i] = maxSoFar.
a.t: O(n) — a single pass over the array with constant work per element.
a.sp: O(1) — the array is modified in place using only two variables.

w: In an interview, mention the brute force briefly, then present the suffix-maximum one-pass solution as the intended answer — it is O(n) time and O(1) space. Common pitfalls: forgetting that the replacement is strictly to the *right* (the current element must not be included in its own max), and overwriting arr[i] before saving it for the max update. Edge cases: single-element arrays (answer [-1]) and non-increasing arrays where every element maps to its immediate right neighbor or -1. Likely follow-ups: do it in place (as shown), handle streaming input, or generalize to 'second greatest element on the right' by tracking the top two values.
